answers.answer: The draw deck is 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards shuffled together. Put 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine spot; set the Gear pawn to 1st; draw 7 cards.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–6 and 9: shuffle the listed cards; place 6 Heat on Engine; set 1st gear; draw 7.

answers.answer: You may stay in your current gear. You may shift two positions, such as 1st to 3rd, by immediately paying 1 Heat during Shift Gears, moving it from Engine to your discard pile. You must have the Heat available then.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Shift Gears: stay or shift one for free; shift two by immediately paying 1 Heat from Engine to discard during this step.

answers.answer: No. In 3rd gear you must play 3 cards, face down.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Play Cards: play cards from hand face down equal to your gear number.

answers.answer: All players do steps 1 and 2 simultaneously, in that order; wait until everyone finishes both before step 3. Then each player completes steps 3–9 before the next begins, in order from the frontmost car. Side-by-side cars: the one closest to the Race Line is ahead and acts first.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Simultaneous Phase and Sequential Phase: all complete steps 1–2 together; each player completes 3–9; Race Line resolves side-by-side order.

answers.answer: Cars do not block passage. If the destination is full, place your car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. When placing, use the spot closest to the Race Line if available.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Blocked Movement: cars never block passage; a full destination puts the car in the first free spot behind. Reveal & Move says use the spot closest to the Race Line if available.

answers.answer: Discard the flipped Heat and Starting Upgrade cards immediately as non-Speed cards. Put the found Speed 3 on top of the played Stress card in the Play Area; the Stress provides speed 3 and remains underneath until Replenish Hand discards both. Resolve all played Stress before Adrenaline.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: discard each flipped non-Speed card; put found Speed on top of played Stress; discard both during Replenish. Resolve Stress before Adrenaline.

answers.answer: The last two cars to move receive Adrenaline because at least 5 cars started. Each gains 1 extra Cooldown and may add 1 speed. The extra speed may be taken before or after Boost. Unused Adrenaline cannot be saved.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Adrenaline: with 5 or more starting cars, last two receive benefits; extra Cooldown and speed; extra speed before or after Boost; unused benefit cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Yes. In React you may use your 2nd-gear Cooldown allowance of 1 to move the Heat card from hand into Engine, then immediately spend it from Engine to Boost. Cooldown and Boost may be activated in any order, and the summary expressly permits cooling Heat then spending it to Boost.
answers.evidence: Actions, Cooldown: 2nd gear has Cooldown 1. React: activate Cooldown and/or Boost in any order; may Cooldown Heat from hand then immediately spend it to Boost.

answers.answer: You may Boost once per turn during React, paying 1 Heat from Engine to discard. Flip from your draw deck, immediately discard non-Speed cards until a Speed card appears; add it to your Play Area and move its value. You cannot choose Boost without Engine Heat available (though you may first Cooldown during React). Boost increases total speed for corner checks.
answers.evidence: Actions, Boost and Paying Heat: once per turn; pay 1 Engine Heat; flip until Speed; add and move its value; Boost counts for corner checks.

answers.answer: Slipstream is optional. The corner check uses speed 6, excluding the 2 Slipstream spaces, so the excess over the limit of 4 is 2 Heat.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Slipstream says optionally move 2 and it does not increase speed for corner checks; Check Corner charges speed minus limit.

answers.answer: Check both corners, in the order crossed, using total speed 8 for each: pay 2 for the limit-6 corner and 4 for the limit-4 corner, 6 Heat altogether.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check every crossed Corner Line in order; compare the same total speed separately to each limit and pay the excess.

answers.answer: The limit-4 corner requires 3 Heat, but only 2 are available, so you cannot pay enough and spin out. Move all remaining Engine Heat to discard and return to the first available space before the corner that caused the spin out. Take 2 extra Stress cards directly into your hand (4th gear); end in 1st gear.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spin Out: insufficient Heat moves all remaining Engine Heat to discard; return before the triggering corner; take 2 Stress in hand in 3rd/4th; set gear to 1st.

answers.answer: You may discard unwanted Speed cards, but not Stress or Heat cards. You may browse neither your own nor another player's discard pile; only the top card of each pile is public knowledge.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Discard: optional unwanted cards, never Stress or Heat; nobody may browse any discard pile; only each top card is public.

answers.answer: Move all Play Area cards to your discard pile, then draw only enough to bring your hand back to 7, not seven additional cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Replenish Hand: move all Play Area cards to discard, then draw only enough to bring hand to 7.

answers.answer: Shuffle your discard pile into a new draw deck immediately, then continue the interrupted Stress flips. Do not include cards still in your Play Area; they have not yet been discarded.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Running Out of Cards: shuffle discard into new deck and continue interrupted flips; do not include Play Area cards.

answers.answer: When paying Heat, move it from Engine to discard. It cycles from discard to draw deck to hand and returns to Engine only via Cooldown. Heat cards cannot normally be played or voluntarily discarded from hand.
answers.evidence: Actions, Paying Heat and Special Rules, Heat Card Cycle: Engine to discard; discard to draw deck to hand; only Cooldown returns it to Engine; hand Heat prohibition.

answers.answer: Commit the two playable cards and fill the two remaining required slots with Heat cards in the Play Area. Move zero spaces; set gear to 1st; discard all committed cards, including the covering Heat, and skip directly to step 9. You cannot use React to Cooldown this turn.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Cluttered Hand: fill missing slots with Heat, move zero, set 1st, discard committed cards, skip to step 9 and React.

answers.answer: The first to cross that round does not automatically win. Among cars finishing in the same round, the car furthest ahead wins; if side by side, closest to Race Line breaks the tie. At round end, remove all cars that crossed the final finish line and place them in finishing order on the Hall of Fame.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: same-round finisher furthest ahead wins, Race Line breaks ties; at round end remove finishers and place in order on Hall of Fame.

answers.answer: No. On the final lap you cannot Slipstream across the finish line or Slipstream after crossing it. After crossing by normal movement, ignore speed limits of corners beyond the finish line and move as far as you can.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: final-lap Slipstream restrictions and exemption from later corner limits.

answers.answer: Both remaining cars receive Adrenaline if they are the last two cars to move. The count is the six cars that started, not the two still racing.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: if race started with 5 or more cars, last two receive benefits; use starting car count even after finishers leave.

answers.answer: Use the lap count printed on the selected board. USA normally uses 2 laps; for a first USA learning race, you may race 1 lap.
answers.evidence: Setup step 1: use laps printed on selected board; first USA learning race may use 1 instead of its normal 2.

answers.answer: Do not assume every track uses exactly 6 Heat and 3 Stress. Check the board for how many Heat and Stress cards each player adds; 6 Heat and 3 Stress are typical.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: check board for each player's Heat and Stress counts, typically 6 Heat and 3 Stress.

answers.answer: Randomly assign cars to the grid, placing them one at a time and filling numbered spots in ascending order. This establishes first-round order; players do not choose preferred starting positions.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8: random assignment, ascending numbered spots, determines first-round order; no player choice of preferred positions.

answers.answer: Place the remaining Stress cards face up near the board as a reserve.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: remaining Stress cards go face up near the board as reserve.

answers.answer: The optional handicap is for the experienced driver to remove 1 or 2 Heat from their own car.
answers.evidence: Setup, Optional handicap: experienced driver may remove 1 or 2 Heat from their own car.

answers.answer: No. The largest shift is two gear positions, for a cost of 1 Heat; 1st to 4th is three positions.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears allows up or down one for free, or two positions by immediately paying 1 Heat; Player Reference gives 1st-to-3rd and 2nd-to-4th examples.

answers.answer: No. A two-position shift costs Heat immediately during Shift Gears, from Engine, and you must have it available then. Heat in hand cooled into Engine during React comes later and cannot pay for that shift.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears: immediately pay during this step and must have Heat available. Paying Heat: hand Heat cannot pay a Heat cost.

answers.answer: Yes, each Stress card is resolved by flipping until a Speed card appears. The total is 3 + 4 + 2 = 9. The found Speed cards are placed on top of their Stress cards from the draw deck; they are not additional cards committed from hand.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: for each Stress card, flip until Speed and put found Speed in Play Area on top; Play Cards requires cards from hand equal to gear.

answers.answer: No. You must move forward exactly the sum of the played card values; you cannot voluntarily stop short to avoid a corner.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move: move exactly that many spaces; cannot voluntarily stop short to avoid a corner.

answers.answer: Use total speed 8, not the 5 spaces moved. For the limit-6 corner, pay 2 Heat if able.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move notes full destination may force shorter movement; Check Corner uses total speed for the round and pays excess over limit.

answers.answer: No. A corner check is triggered by crossing a Corner Line; being near one without crossing it does not require payment.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Track Lines: a Corner Line triggers a check when crossed; Check Corner applies to crossed lines.

answers.answer: At speed 6 or below the limit, no Heat is due, so an empty Engine does not by itself cause a spin out. Spin Out applies when you cannot pay required Heat for a corner.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: pay excess, if any; if speed does not exceed limit, pay nothing. Spin Out requires inability to pay enough for a corner.

answers.answer: You successfully pay the 3 Heat and continue; having no Heat left afterward does not itself cause a spin out.
answers.evidence: Paying Heat moves the specified amount from Engine to discard. Spin Out is when you cannot pay enough for the corner.

answers.answer: Pay 2 Heat at the limit-6 corner, leaving 3. The limit-4 corner requires 4, so it causes the spin out. Move the remaining 3 Heat to discard and return to the first available space before that second corner. Take 2 Stress directly into your hand and set gear to 1st.
answers.evidence: Check Corner charges each corner's excess separately; Spin Out: remaining Engine Heat to discard; return before causing corner; 2 Stress in hand for 3rd/4th; gear to 1st.

answers.answer: Take 1 extra Stress card directly into your hand and end in 1st gear.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 1 Stress in hand when in 1st/2nd gear, then move Gear pawn to 1st.

answers.answer: 1st gear provides Cooldown 3, and Adrenaline adds 1, for up to 4 Heat moved from hand to Engine. Cooling is available/optional, not forced; you may activate available symbols during React.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: 1st gear Cooldown 3. Adrenaline gives 1 extra Cooldown. React says activate available Cooldown and/or Boost symbols.

answers.answer: Yes. The extra speed is optional (you may add it), while the extra Cooldown is also available; you can use the Cooldown and decline the speed.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: gains access to 1 extra Cooldown and may add 1 extra speed.

answers.answer: Yes, the last car to move is eligible even if it ends in the lead, because eligibility is assigned by last-to-move order. In a four-car race the second-to-last car does not get Adrenaline; the two-car benefit applies only when 5 or more cars started.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: last car to move gets benefits; last two only when race started with 5 or more cars.

answers.answer: You qualify if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car. If neither applies, you do not qualify.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car, optionally move 2 spaces.

answers.answer: Yes. Slipstream eligibility is checked at the Slipstream step, after React; if Boost leaves you immediately behind a car then, you qualify.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure orders React as step 5 and Slipstream as step 6; Slipstream condition is based on where you end at that step.

answers.answer: You get one optional two-space Slipstream move, not two moves or four spaces.
answers.evidence: Slipstream says if you end next to another car or immediately behind a car, optionally move 2 spaces forward.

answers.answer: Slipstream does not permit sharing an occupied spot. A full landing space uses the normal Blocked Movement rule, placing you in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. Any shorter movement does not change corner-check speed.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: full landing uses normal Blocked Movement, no sharing, and shorter movement does not change corner-check speed.

answers.answer: No. The final finish-line exemption applies only to corners beyond it. Pay 4 Heat for the limit-4 corner before the line; ignore the limit-3 corner beyond the line, for 4 Heat total.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: after crossing final finish line, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it. Check Corner charges excess for crossed corners.

answers.answer: Yes. On an intermediate lap, an otherwise legal Slipstream may cross the start/finish line, and normal corner speed limits still apply beyond it.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: intermediate-lap legal Slipstream may cross start/finish; normal corner limits apply beyond it.

answers.answer: They continue racing; at the end of each round, remove cars that crossed the final finish line and place them in finishing order. Continue until all cars finish.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: remove finishers at round end; continue playing until all cars finish.

answers.answer: No. In the core game, crossing a Corner Line triggers a corner check. The Legends Line is used only in advanced play; crossing it alone does not trigger core-game corner payment.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Track Lines: Corner Line triggers in core; Legends Line only advanced, not a core payment trigger.

answers.answer: No. You choose your gear during Shift Gears before committing cards. If you shift down to 2nd, you commit 2 cards; having started the round in 3rd does not make this a Cluttered Hand if you have two playable cards.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure orders Shift Gears before Play Cards, and Play Cards count equals current gear; Cluttered Hand applies when too few playable cards for your gear.
